heroHeadline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: China AI Chip Market 'Largely Conceded' to Huawei — Alibaba Zhenwu M890 Claims 3x Nvidia H20 as Domestic Stack Achieves Structural Permanence
heroSubtitle: May 21, 2026 — In back-to-back developments that mark a structural milestone in the US-China tech decoupling, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly acknowledged on May 21 that the company has 'largely conceded' China's AI chip market to Huawei, describing the export ban as having 'largely backfired' commercially. Nvidia's Q1 FY2027 earnings reached $81.62B (+85% YoY) with China data center revenue near-zero — down from 20%+ of total historically. The previous day (May 20), Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu M890 AI accelerator at its Cloud Summit in Hangzhou, claiming 3x performance over the Nvidia H20 with 560,000+ units already shipped to 400+ enterprise customers across 20 industries. The Zhenwu M890 (144GB HBM3, 800GB/s interchip bandwidth) is the first domestic Chinese chip to publicly claim performance above the H20 ceiling — the chip calibrated to be 'sufficient but not dangerous.' Together, these two events close the loop on China's domestic AI chip transition: DeepSeek V4 runs natively on Huawei Ascend, ByteDance committed $5.6B to Huawei Ascend 950PR, Cambricon posted its first-ever profitable year, CATL holds 47.2% of China's EV battery market, and China shipped ~90% of global humanoid robots in 2025. The CEO of the world's most valuable semiconductor company has now confirmed on the record what China's technology data has been showing for months: the domestic AI chip ecosystem built under US sanctions pressure has achieved structural permanence.
